title: Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry over Rice

qty.note: rounds off the tomatoes' acidity - do not skip
about 1 3/4 cups cooked; freshly cooked or leftover both work

steps.text: Break the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of the salt, and beat with chopsticks or a fork until completely uniform.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a wok over medium-high until it shimmers.

Pour in the eggs, let them puff for a few seconds, then push with the spatula into soft curds. A thermometer reads 160°F (71°C) while the curds still look a little glossy - pull them out at that point.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Slide the eggs onto a plate, leaving the fat in the wok.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic; stir for 15 seconds until fragrant - back the wok off the heat if it darkens.
Add the tomato wedges and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the rest of the salt and all the sugar; keep the pieces moving so they release juice but hold shape.
Pour the soy sauce down the side of the wok and toss; simmer 1 minute until the juices thicken enough to lightly coat a spoon.
Return the eggs and fold twice - keep the curds in big pieces or they will shred into the sauce.
Off the heat, fold in the white pepper and most of the green onions.
Mound hot rice on two plates, spoon the stir-fry alongside with its juices, and finish with the remaining green onions.
